authors: Jean-Baptiste Tristan (principal developer) and Markus de Medeiros, with other contributors
title: SampCert, explained
h1: SampCert: verified random samplers and differential privacy in Lean 4, as deployed in AWS Clean Rooms
lead: SampCert proves that its discrete Gaussian and discrete Laplace samplers, built from nothing but random bytes, output exactly the distributions they claim, and that the noise mechanisms built on them are differentially private. The privacy results cover pure DP, zero-concentrated DP (zCDP) and (ε, δ)-DP, adaptive composition, histograms and the AboveThreshold (sparse vector) algorithm. A text search finds no sorry or axiom. What is not proved is that the C++ code that runs the samplers (random bytes, bind, loops) matches the Lean definitions, and the Lean was not built for this site.
desc: An unofficial plain-English tour of SampCert (Jean-Baptiste Tristan, Markus de Medeiros and contributors): exact correctness of a discrete Gaussian sampler, the zCDP Gaussian mechanism, adaptive composition, the zCDP-to-(ε, δ) conversion, a generic private histogram and a pure-DP AboveThreshold.
startNote: Start with the sampler: the discrete Gaussian sampler is exact, after a look at what an SLang program is. Then the privacy side: what zCDP means, the Gaussian mechanism, composition and the conversion to (ε, δ)-DP. The DPSystem interface explains how one proof covers both pure DP and zCDP, which the histogram uses. AboveThreshold is the longest single privacy proof.
sizeNote: About 18,500 lines of Lean in 108 files. This site scans the 92 files of the sampler and privacy library under SampCert/ (about 17,100 lines) and explains its main thread; the Dafny/Python extractor, tests and FFI glue are described but not explained.
agentCtx: SampCert (leanprover/SampCert): a Lean 4 + Mathlib library of verified random samplers (uniform, Bernoulli, exp(-γ), discrete Laplace, discrete Gaussian) written in a probability monad SLang, plus a differential-privacy framework (pure DP, zCDP, approximate DP) with verified composition, post-processing and queries (histograms, bounded mean, AboveThreshold, sparse vector), deployed in AWS Clean Rooms.

gloss.PMF: Mathlib's probability mass function: a function into [0, ∞] whose values sum to 1.
gloss.ENNReal: Extended nonnegative reals [0, ∞] (ℝ≥0∞), where probabilities and infinite sums live.
gloss.ENNReal.ofReal: Converts a real number to [0, ∞], sending negatives to 0.
gloss.HasSum: HasSum f a: the (possibly infinite) series Σ f(x) converges to a.
gloss.Countable: The type has at most countably many elements.
gloss.Inhabited: The type has a designated element.
gloss.MeasurableSpace: A σ-algebra of measurable sets; here always all subsets.
gloss.MeasurableSingletonClass: Every single point is a measurable set.
gloss.List: Finite lists; a dataset is a List of records.
gloss.Fin: Fin n is the type of numbers 0, …, n−1.
gloss.discrim: Mathlib's discriminant b² − 4ac of a quadratic.
